C001.reason: The name field is being read from the decoded v1 entity and included in observations. With the schema change, name is removed from v1 Entity, so this read must be eliminated.

C002.reason: The v1 Entity construction includes a name field that no longer exists in the new schema. This must be removed to match the new v1 schema which only has entity_id.

edits.before: const fields = { entity_id: entity.entityId, ...(version === "v1" ? { name: (entity as EntityV1).name } : {}) };

rationale: Removed Entity.name from v1 construction and observations. The v1 schema no longer includes the name field (field 2 is reserved). The processEntity function now only extracts entity_id from decoded entities for both versions. The test payload construction for v1 no longer includes name. The subscribe flow will decode v1 payloads (including legacy ones with field 2) but the generated bindings will ignore the reserved field, so entity_id is preserved while name is simply not present in the decoded object.
assumptions: Generated TypeScript bindings for v1 Entity after buf generate will have only entityId property, no name property
Decoding a legacy v1 payload containing field 2 (name) will preserve entity_id and silently drop the unknown/reserved field per protobuf semantics
The subscribe flow's processEntity call for v1 topics will work with both old and new payloads
v2 Entity construction and observations remain unchanged as intended
